text:
Same structural issue as PKIX-fmtv.17 (just human-labeled in this session). The acceptance criterion is a per-purpose pass-rate baseline. PKITS chains uniformly fail through verify_* wrappers because PKITS EE certs lack any EKU and any SAN (verified ValidCertificatePathTest1EE.crt). pkix-difftest's existing PEM-tree / limbo / PKITS corpora are chain-shape-only.

The curated EKU+SAN-bearing corpus that .17 was supposed to deliver is a precondition for a substantive .18 deliverable. Without it, this bead can run differential oracles only against the 8 small unit-test fixtures in pkix-chain/tests/fixtures/ — 8 data points is a smoke test, not a per-purpose pass-rate baseline.

Two coherent paths:

(A) WAIT FOR CURATED CORPUS: hold this bead blocked-on-deps until a curated corpus exists (whether produced under a rescoped .17 or a new bead). This is the AGENTS.md-aligned framing: the acceptance criterion (pass-rate over a corpus) implies a corpus.

(B) RESCOPE DOWN: shrink this bead to "OpenSSL-as-oracle smoke test against the 8 existing pkix-chain fixtures, document per-wrapper agreement." Cheap to do, low value, locks in a non-baseline shape for the future baseline. Not recommended.

The dependency on .17 (or its successor) is structural, not formal — bd ready will continue to surface .18 even though it cannot meet its own acceptance. Recommend labeling human and waiting for the .17 decision to settle the corpus story, then either filing a new dep edge or rescoping this bead accordingly.

Releasing without claiming. Labeling human.
